article.title: ワンピース
article.part: Contraste Guatemala–Japón — グアテマラと日本語の対照
article.chapter: Préstamos engañosos y equivalencias falsas — 紛らわしい外来語・偽の対応

claims.summary: Japanese ワンピース has a clothing sense for a woman’s or girl’s garment in which the upper part and skirt are continuous; Daijisen also separately records a general one-part sense.

English one-piece may be an adjective for clothing made in one piece and a noun for a one-piece swimsuit, so the Japanese dress sense should not be translated mechanically as the literal phrase “one piece”.
Kotobank’s Seisen entry records 赤いワン・ピイスを着た女は from Akutagawa’s 1927 歯車 as an early attestation of the garment sense.

locator.description: Kotobank, lines 16–23, デジタル大辞泉: sense 1 defines clothing with upper garment and skirt continuous for women/children; sense 2 “もの” formed from a single part. Lines 35–42, 改訂新版 世界大百科事典: identifies women’s/children’s clothing and allows fabric or waist seams.

links.notes: Scope is attributed to named lexicographic entries; no claim that all garments have identical patterns or construction.

locator.description: Collins English Dictionary, lines 216–232: adjective for a clothing article consisting of one piece; noun specifically a woman’s bathing suit. Compare Kotobank lines 20–21 for the distinct Japanese dress sense and the separate general one-part sense.

links.notes: The article describes dictionary senses, not all English usage; “vestido” is grounded in the Japanese entry.

locator.description: Kotobank, lines 28–33, 精選版 日本国語大辞典: first attestation example 赤いワン・ピイスを着た女は, cited from 歯車 (1927), by 芥川龍之介.

links.notes: The brief Japanese excerpt is quoted exactly from the dictionary’s cited example.
